cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 answers T4's patience with its cost; T6 replies 'Fair, so I narrow it'.
cells.limitation: T10 absorbs T9 without engaging it; Checklist Keeper rarely answers a direct objection.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 adds non-product causes absent from openings; T6 turns bare-skin period into that test.
cells.limitation: T8 motive speculation adds little that later turns build on beyond T9.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Patience versus cost (T4-T5) and order bias versus efficiency (T11-T12) examined.
cells.limitation: T5 raises stacked exfoliants, but one-at-a-time protocol never addresses combination-only reactions.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T12 concedes blind-ish order yet keeps suspect-first; disagreement left standing.
cells.limitation: Checklist Keeper's T7 triage and T10 protocol are never challenged or reshaped.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D ends with a clear protocol and a sharpened open question on test order.
cells.limitation: Section D lists how long to wait as disputed, but no turn argued it.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T12 restates T11's bias case accurately before keeping its own efficiency point.
cells.limitation: T9 sets aside T8's motive point briskly rather than at its strongest.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 names the assumption 'the cause is in the three'; T6 answers with a test.
cells.limitation: Nobody tests T10's jaw patch as representative of the stinging area.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T7 and Section E list hives, swelling, breathing trouble as reasons for professional care.
cells.limitation: T3 'Irritated skin makes for poor memory' is an unsupported, garbled claim (observed).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section A separates reported timing and sting from the unknown culprit; T1 calls guesses hypotheses.
cells.limitation: T7 says tingling 'points to irritation' without noting some actives sting expectedly.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 'Fair, so I narrow it'; T12 'I concede part of that'.
cells.limitation: Bias Spotter never concedes anything, including T9's point that motive does not change step one.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames the concern as cause-finding plus whether the sting is dangerous.
cells.limitation: T8's 'why the question' motive detour fits a troubleshooting request loosely.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: Three products started together drives T4's point that a log cannot separate them.
cells.limitation: The one-week timing is never used to argue anything about reaction type.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T9: calm skin versus keeping the routine 'is theirs to settle'.
cells.limitation: The user's goal of keeping some products is assumed, not checked (T5, T9).

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 names weeks without paid products on raw skin; T7 flags safety stakes.
cells.limitation: T2 and T5 lean on price as a factor the user never mentioned.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T7 and Section E branch on sting appearance and on persistence on bare skin.
cells.limitation: No turn asks what the three products are or contain, e.g. acids or retinoids.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T8 offers wasted money, routine attachment, trusted recommendation as alternatives, none asserted.
cells.limitation: T8's motives are not posed as a question; Section D asks a different one.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 vivid-suspect bias, T5 'you assumed the cause is in the three', T11 confirmation.
cells.limitation: The assumption that stinging always means something is wrong is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T9 names calm skin soon versus keeping the full routine; Section D repeats it.
cells.limitation: The value conflict appears in one turn and is not developed further.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T8 names fear of waste and a trusted recommender without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Worry about lasting skin damage is not acknowledged beyond T7's triage list.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T9 leaves the ranking to the user; Section D leaves test order open for them.
cells.limitation: Section D's reflection question is offered once without options to refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Options span pause, reintroduce, check other causes, seek care (T1, T5, T7, Section E).
cells.limitation: A limited step, pausing only the likeliest suspect, is never weighed against stopping all three.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T5 prices the clean test in weeks and raw skin; T12 weighs efficiency against bias.
cells.limitation: The cost of going straight to a pharmacist is never weighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T6: sting fades on bare skin favors products; stays favors other causes.
cells.limitation: The order dispute in T11-T12 gets no observable condition that would settle it.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names sting appearance and other changes as the decisive unknowns.
cells.limitation: Gap length between reintroductions left vague in T4 and T10 without saying whether it matters.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T10: gentle basics, one product, small patch, log, repeat; Section E escalation path.
cells.limitation: 'Several days' in T4 and T10 is left undefined for a reader to act on.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: Plain wording throughout: 'Simple steps get done; elaborate ones get dropped' (T10).
cells.limitation: T3 'Irritated skin makes for poor memory' reads ambiguously.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 'That patience' clearly points to T4; T12 'that' clearly points to T11.
cells.limitation: T6 'my hypothesis' is unclear: T1's guilty-product guess or T5's in-the-three assumption.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within the word range; short sections around them.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Experimenter tests, Bias Spotter guards order, Checklist Keeper triages; T6 and T12 mark shifts.
cells.limitation: Bias Spotter and Checklist Keeper overlap in T2-T3, both distrusting the guess.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section D recap is short and adds the open dispute.
cells.limitation: Section E repeats T7's symptom list almost word for word.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T7 raises the stakes: allergic signs mean dropping the experiment entirely.
cells.limitation: Tension stays low-key; the safety stake gets one turn, then fades.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T12 names what moved it, 'a blind-ish order protects against wishful reading'.
cells.limitation: Both shifts (T6, T12) are partial narrowings, not surprising turns.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T2 'Careful, you already have a suspect forming' gives the Bias Spotter edge.
cells.limitation: Checklist Keeper's voice stays procedural and flat in T3, T7 and T10.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T2 'Minds crave a single villain'; T4 'or the result is mush'.
cells.limitation: No analogy or vivid example anchors the protocol in T6-T10.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T7 'the missing fact that reorders everything' builds forward momentum.
cells.limitation: Emotional register stays even; the user's discomfort is barely felt after T5.

strengths: T5 names the hidden assumption that the cause is among the three; T6 turns it into a bare-skin test.
T7 and Section E branch on what the sting looks like, with a clear path to professional care.
T11-T12 argue test order on its merits, with a named concession and an honestly unresolved dispute.
weaknesses: No mind asks what the three products contain, which would change the prime suspect (C3.5).
T5's stacked exfoliants point is dropped; the one-at-a-time plan never handles combination reactions (C1.3).
T8's motive detour by the Bias Spotter fits a troubleshooting question loosely and is not posed as a question.

symptoms.observed: No turn asks which products or actives were started, though this ranks suspects.
symptoms.evidence: Stacked exfoliants, a new detergent, cold weather could each produce

symptoms.observed: Product interaction raised in T5, never reconciled with single-product reintroduction in T10.
symptoms.evidence: add one product, try it on a small patch like the jaw

symptoms.observed: Motive speculation inserted into a practical troubleshooting question.
symptoms.evidence: Another unknown is why the question is how to figure it out.

symptoms.observed: Unsupported causal claim about irritated skin and memory.
symptoms.evidence: Irritated skin makes for poor memory.

symptoms.observed: Gap length called disputed in Section D but never argued or bounded.
symptoms.evidence: with a gap of several days, or the result is mush

findings.description: The claim that irritated skin makes for poor memory is unsupported and reads as a garbled rationale for logging.
Attributions to Popper, Kahneman and Gawande are general and consistent with those works but cannot be verified here; no quotations are used.

rubric_fit_notes: For a practical skincare troubleshooting question, criterion 4 (self-discovery) fits loosely; the debate's motive and values turns (T8, T9) are partly there to serve it. Medical accuracy was judged from general knowledge only.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision (troubleshooting) question, so every cell was read as written, with criterion 5 weighted on diagnostic conditions and escalation thresholds.
